procedure_column: Liu et al. 2016 (M&PS 51) Tissint martian meteorite Silicates, oxides & glass Spot analysis LA-Q-ICP-MS Virginia Tech

Technique.cell: LA-ICP-MS (193 nm excimer laser + ICP-MS; top-level technique) [P4]
Technique.value: LA-ICP-MS (193 nm excimer laser + ICP-MS; top-level technique) [P4]

Procedure Reference(s).cell: Udry et al. (2012) and Pernet-Fisher et al. (2014) cited as broad references for the analytical procedure [P4]
Procedure Reference(s).value: Udry et al. (2012) and Pernet-Fisher et al. (2014) cited as broad references for the analytical procedure [P4]

Coupling Description.cell: EPMA provides major element concentrations for comparison with LA-ICP-MS oxide-sum normalization results; agreement within <10% verified [P4]
Coupling Description.value: EPMA provides major element concentrations for comparison with LA-ICP-MS oxide-sum normalization results; agreement within <10% verified [P4]

Target Material.cell: Martian meteorite (Tissint) silicates, oxides, and glass: olivine, low-Ca pyroxene, augite, maskelynite, Fe-Ti-Cr oxides, shock melt glass, fusion crust [P4]

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Phase > Spot — "The time-lapse plots of each spot were examined, and only the plateau region was used to quantify the trace element abundances" (p.4); abundances are reported as per-phase means ("n = 7", "n = 13", table p.9), the individual spots being in a supplement not in the archived PDF

Sample Preparation Method.cell: N (not described; sections mentioned; polished implied) [P4]
Sample Preparation Method.value: N (not described; sections mentioned; polished implied) [P4]

Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.cell: N — spots are screened after the fact, not before: "The time-lapse plots of each spot were examined, and only the plateau region was used to quantify the trace element abundances" (p.4). That is a rejection rule (see `Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteria`), not a rule for choosing units

Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.cell: Petrographic microscopy, SEM and EMP — "The petrography of these sections was examined using a petrographic microscope and a scanning electron microscope", followed by BSE images and element maps (p.3); the EMP results then serve as internal standards for the ablation data, which are normalised using "EMP CaO or MgO values" for silicates and "40Ca counts to CaO concentrations from the EMP analysis" for phosphate (p.4)

Laser Manufacturer & Model.cell: GeoLasPro (193 nm Excimer laser-ablation system; manufacturer not stated by name; GeoLasPro is a Lambda Physik/Coherent product) [P4]
Laser Manufacturer & Model.value: GeoLasPro (193 nm Excimer laser-ablation system; manufacturer not stated by name; GeoLasPro is a Lambda Physik/Coherent product) [P4]

ICP-MS Type.cell: N (quadrupole implied by Agilent 7500ce model; not explicitly stated in paper) [P4]
ICP-MS Type.value: N (quadrupole implied by Agilent 7500ce model; not explicitly stated in paper) [P4]

Mass Resolution Setting.value: N (unit resolution implied for quadrupole; not explicitly stated) [P4]

Data Processing Software(s).value: AMS ver. 1.0 (Mutchler et al. 2008; Analysis Management System, stand-alone software) [P4]

Laser Spot Geometry.cell: 24 and 32 µm diameter (commonly used for silicates and glass); 90 µm (some olivine analyses to evaluate low REE signal sampling) [P4]

Laser Fluence (Energy Density).cell: 7–10 J/m² (stated in paper; units as written; likely a typographic error for J/cm²) [P4]
Laser Fluence (Energy Density).value: 7–10 J/m² (stated in paper; units as written; likely a typographic error for J/cm²) [P4]

Laser Pulse Duration.value: N (ns excimer system; pulse duration not stated) [P4]

Analysis Sequence.cell: NIST 610 glass standard analyzed before and after every session; unknowns in between [P4]
Analysis Sequence.value: NIST 610 glass standard analyzed before and after every session; unknowns in between [P4]

Target Species.cell: N (not explicitly listed in methods; results text mentions Sc, V, Ti, Co, Ni, REEs measured in silicates; full isotope list not stated) [P4, P7, P11]

value.member: N (not explicitly listed in methods; results text mentions Sc, V, Ti, Co, Ni, REEs measured in silicates; full isotope list not stated) [P4, P7, P11]

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species

Reported Variables and Units.cell: Trace element abundances per phase (ppm, with REE at ppb level — "8 ppb La, 23 ppb Yb, and 6 ppb Lu", "Nickel contents in olivines decrease from 910 ppm at Mg# = ~80 to 234 ppm", p.7), reported as means with 1σ and n (table p.9); limits of detection are reported per element (Table 3, p.9). Silicate and oxide abundances are normalised to 100 wt% oxide total; phosphate to EMP CaO (p.4)

value.member: reported as means with 1σ and n
limits of detection are reported per element (Table 3, p.9). Silicate and oxide abundances are normalised to 100 wt% oxide total

Background Count Time.cell: 50 s (background counted for 50 s before each LA-ICP-MS analysis) [P4]
Background Count Time.value: 50 s (background counted for 50 s before each LA-ICP-MS analysis) [P4]

Internal Standard Approach.cell: Normalization to 100 wt% oxide total (for silicates and oxides) [P4]

Elemental Fractionation Correction.cell: External calibration using NIST 610 glass standard analyzed before and after session; oxide-sum normalization corrects for ablation yield variation; no explicit downhole fractionation correction described [P4]

Matrix Offset Correction (LIEF).cell: N (not stated; agreement within <10% between oxide-sum normalization and EMP-based IS noted as validation) [P4]
Matrix Offset Correction (LIEF).value: N (not stated; agreement within <10% between oxide-sum normalization and EMP-based IS noted as validation) [P4]

Signal Integration Interval Method.cell: Time-lapse plots of each spot examined; only the plateau region used to quantify trace element abundances [P4]
Signal Integration Interval Method.value: Time-lapse plots of each spot examined; only the plateau region used to quantify trace element abundances [P4]

Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach.cell: N (not explicitly stated; implied by plateau-region selection excluding non-stable intervals) [P4]
Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach.value: N (not explicitly stated; implied by plateau-region selection excluding non-stable intervals) [P4]

Blank / Background Correction Method.cell: 50 s background measurement before each analysis; background subtracted (method not explicitly described beyond counting duration) [P4]
Blank / Background Correction Method.value: 50 s background measurement before each analysis; background subtracted (method not explicitly described beyond counting duration) [P4]

Normalization / Standards-Based Correcti.cell: 100% oxide total normalization applied per analysis for silicates and oxides; NIST 610 used for external calibration before and after session [P4]

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially — the reported values are means of stated counts ("n = 7", "n = 13", table p.9). No acceptance or rejection rule is stated; the plateau-region screening of each spot is signal-based and is recorded under Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach

Combination Method.cell: all: average of n LA-ICP-MS analyses per glass type — Table 3 note d: 'Average of a number of LA-ICP-MS analysis'

value.value: average of n LA-ICP-MS analyses per glass type

Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.cell: NIST 610 glass standard analyzed before and after every session [P4]
Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.value: NIST 610 glass standard analyzed before and after every session [P4]

Detection Limit.cell: Referenced in Table 3 and Table S1; specific values not directly stated in main text; REE in olivines below detection limits at 24–32 µm conditions [P4, P7, P11]

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: For silicates: oxide-sum normalization agrees within <10% with EMP-based IS method (internal cross-check, not a separate QC standard) [P4]

members: For silicates: oxide-sum normalization agrees within <10% with EMP-based IS method (internal cross-check, not a separate QC standard)

Additional Notes.cell: Paper broadly follows Udry et al. (2012) and Pernet-Fisher et al. (2014) for procedure; two IS approaches used for different mineral phases (oxide-sum for silicates; EMP CaO for phosphate); 90 µm spot used on some olivines to evaluate whether low REE signals result from insufficient sampling volume [P4]
